manager.name: Doreen Pike
manager.title: Head of Hot Beverages
manager.personality: fiercely protective of the good mugs
quips: Hands off the good mugs. I've got them numbered.
Kettle's been on since 1979. Never once let me down.
A proper brew is three minutes. Not two. Not four. Three.
Those desks won't fill themselves. Hire someone, love.

arrival.text: Ah, the new starter! HR said you'd be down. I'm Doreen. Kettle's that way.
Lovely to meet you. Where do I start?
Fourteen teas, two sugars, one oat milk. Tap the kettle if they get impatient.
Got it. Hands off the good mugs?
Clever one. Upgrade the tea round and you'll be upstairs before the biscuits run out.

manager.name: Stan Okafor
manager.title: Post Room Supervisor
manager.personality: has a nickname for every pigeonhole
quips: 'Urgent' in red biro? Goes to the bottom. House rule.
Pigeonhole 14 bites. Long story. Wear gloves.
I can tell a gas bill by the smell. It's a gift.
Upgrade the sorting desk and I'll name a pigeonhole after you.

arrival.text: Fresh up from the kitchen? Doreen says you make a mean brew. I'm Stan.
Word travels fast round here.
Not as fast as the post. Every letter in this building comes through these hands.
So... where do these go?
Pigeonholes, A to Z. Tap the sorting desk when the pile wobbles. Mind the franker.

manager.name: Gwen Llewellyn
manager.title: Print Room Manager
manager.personality: speaks fluent error code
quips: Margaret's humming. That means she's happy. Or about to explode.
PC LOAD LETTER? She's just being dramatic.
Toner on your shirt is a badge of honour down here.
Tap her when she sulks. Firmly, but with love.

arrival.text: Duck! Sorry, she spits toner when she's nervous. I'm Gwen. You're the promotion?
That's me. Is the copier... alive?
Practically. Her name's Margaret. Treat her nicely and the memos fly out.
And if she jams?
Tap her firmly to hurry things along. And upgrade her. She likes attention.

manager.name: Bernard Fisk
manager.title: Keeper of the Cupboard
manager.personality: has never once lent out a stapler
quips: That stapler? Signed out to me. Permanently.
Someone took a green highlighter in March. I haven't forgotten.
Every biro has a serial number. I wrote them on myself.
Restock the shelves before the sticky notes revolt.

arrival.text: Sign in, please. Nobody enters the stationery store without signing the ledger.
With which pen?
Your own. Pens leave this cupboard over my dead body. Name's Bernard.
So my job is... guarding biros?
Stocking them. Keep the shelves full and upgrade often. Golden paperclips? Don't ask.

manager.name: Priya Mistry
manager.title: Switchboard Supervisor
manager.personality: can hold six calls and a conversation
quips: Synergex plc, please hold... sorry, habit.
The hold music is a pan pipe medley. I chose it. You're welcome.
I once transferred a call to the canteen by accident. He stayed.
Busy lines mean busy business. Hire another operator!

arrival.text: Synergex plc, how may I direct your... oh! You're the new one. Priya. Headset's yours.
Do I just press the flashing lights?
All of them, eventually. Every call is important. Some more than others.
Which ones?
Ones from upstairs. Tap the switchboard when the queue builds. Never say 'hang on'.

manager.name: Marjorie Thwaite
manager.title: Chief Filing Officer
manager.personality: alphabetises her packed lunch
quips: I filed my birthday card under B. For Brilliant.
Misfiled is just lost with extra steps.
Drawer three sticks. Lift, wiggle, pull. Like a lock.
Fill those empty desks. The cabinets are getting lonely.

arrival.text: Welcome to Admin! I've filed your arrival under A. For Arrival. Marjorie Thwaite.
Very organised.
Very. Every report at Synergex ends up in these cabinets. Eventually.
And my job is to make that sooner?
Precisely. Upgrade the filing and you'll be upstairs before I've cross-referenced you.

manager.name: Babs Delaney
manager.title: Typing Pool Supervisor
manager.personality: types 140 words a minute while chatting
quips: Ding! That's the sound of productivity, love.
Yours faithfully, yours sincerely. Know the difference.
Correction fluid fumes? Character building.
Upgrade the pool. We could hit two hundred words a minute.

arrival.text: Shh! Hear that? Forty typewriters in perfect rhythm. Gorgeous. I'm Babs.
It's very... loud.
It's music, love. Every letter Synergex sends goes out from this pool.
I can do about thirty words a minute.
We'll fix that. Upgrade the pool and tap to hurry when the in-tray piles up.

manager.name: Kevin Osei
manager.title: Data Entry Team Lead
manager.personality: keeps a spreadsheet of his spreadsheets
quips: Row 9,001 is where the magic happens. Allegedly.
I dream in tab-separated values. It's restful.
Never trust a cell that says 'see attached'.
More keyboards, more clacking. Hire someone, please.

arrival.text: You must be the new keystroke. Kevin. Data Entry. We put numbers in boxes.
Which numbers?
All of them. The screens hum, the keyboards clack, and the database grows.
Sounds hypnotic.
It is. Upgrade the team, and if anyone asks for 'a quick favour', run.

manager.name: Ambrose Hale
manager.title: Senior Archivist
manager.personality: has not seen daylight since 1994
quips: That box is from 1987. Do not open. I mean it.
Daylight? I've read about it. Sounds overrated.
Every invoice tells a story. Mostly about invoices.
The dust won't shelve itself. Neither will the boxes.

arrival.text: Ah. A visitor. We don't get many. I'm Ambrose. I keep the past in order.
It's very dusty up here.
History is dusty. Every box has a story. Most of them are invoices.
What do I do with them?
Label, box, shelve. Upgrade the archive and the dust settles itself.

manager.name: Fiona Grant
manager.title: Office Manager
manager.personality: runs the calendar with an iron fist
quips: Room 3 is double-booked. It's always double-booked.
I booked the fire drill. Then the fire. Then the fire brigade.
Nobody takes my laminator. Nobody.
Upgrade the bookings desk before the away day becomes a riot.

arrival.text: Right on time. I like that. Fiona Grant, Office Manager. I book the rooms.
All of them?
Every single one. Board meetings, away days, the fire drill. Even the fire.
What if two teams want the same room?
Diplomacy. And biscuits. Upgrade the bookings desk and the clashes sort themselves.

manager.name: Dev Kapoor
manager.title: IT Helpdesk Lead
manager.personality: asks if you've tried turning it off
quips: Have you tried turning it off and on again? Not you. The printer.
Don't look at the fax machine. It knows.
My ticket queue is empty. I don't trust it.
Printers fear upgrades. That's why we do them.

arrival.text: Have you tried turning it off and on again? Sorry, reflex. Dev, IT Helpdesk.
I'm the new promotion.
Brilliant. The printers here are possessed. Not metaphorically.
How do I fix a possessed printer?
Same as anything. Tap it, upgrade it, and never make eye contact with the fax.

manager.name: Zara Quinn
manager.title: Head of Infrastructure
manager.personality: thinks the servers have feelings
quips: Shh. They're sleeping. That's what the blinking means.
It's always the cable at the back. Always.
Rack seven sings when it's happy. Rack nine never sings.
Fans wheezing? Tap the job. They like the attention.

arrival.text: Close the door, you're letting the cold out. Zara. I look after the machines.
It's freezing in here!
They like it that way. Forty racks, blinking happily. Mostly happily.
And when they stop blinking?
You reboot them. Gently. Upgrade the racks and tap when the fans start wheezing.

manager.name: Graham Petty
manager.title: Spreadsheet Team Lead
manager.personality: colour-codes his feelings
quips: Never merge cells. That way lies madness.
Green means good. Red means meeting. Amber means panic.
A circular reference walked in here once. Never left.
Upgrade the team and the formulas practically write themselves.

arrival.text: Ah, our new cell! Graham. I've given you a row. Row 47. Don't merge it.
Merge it? Why would I...?
People do. Terrible things happen. Circular references. Hash errors.
I'll stick to my row.
Wise. Upgrade the team and the formulas will practically write themselves.

manager.name: Big Terry
manager.title: Facilities Manager
manager.personality: carries a toolbox to every meeting
quips: That drip has been dripping since the Coronation. Of someone.
The lift has moods. Today it's sulking at floor nine.
Every radiator sings a different note. I've named them all.
More hands, fewer leaks. Hire another fixer-upper.

arrival.text: Alright? Terry. Facilities. If it's broken, leaking or squeaking, it's mine.
That sounds like a lot.
Old building, mate. The lift's got moods and the radiators sing.
Where do I start?
Grab a ladder. Upgrade the team and tap the job when the drips get dramatic.

manager.name: Hilary Bloom
manager.title: Health & Safety Officer
manager.personality: wears a hard hat indoors, just in case
quips: That chair has four legs. Have you assessed all four?
A biro is a stabbing hazard if you believe in yourself.
Fire drill Thursday. Bring a sensible cardigan.
Clipboard's full. Tap the job before it overflows. Safely.

arrival.text: Stop! Before you step off that lift: have you read the induction booklet?
There's a booklet?
There are eleven. I'm Hilary. Nothing here happens without a risk assessment.
Even making tea?
Especially making tea. Upgrade the assessments and tap when the clipboard's full.

manager.name: Clive Hargreaves
manager.title: Head of Meetings
manager.personality: has never ended a meeting early
quips: This meeting could have been an email. So could that one.
Any Other Business? There's always Other Business.
Five minutes, I said. Two hours, it was. Lovely.
Upgrade the meetings and they might finish on time. Might.

arrival.text: Welcome to Management! We have a quick five-minute catch-up. It's two hours.
What's on the agenda?
Agreeing the agenda. Then a meeting about the meeting. Then biscuits.
When does the actual work happen?
In meetings, mostly. Upgrade them and they'll start finishing on time. Allegedly.

manager.name: Agnes Okonkwo
manager.title: Head of Secretariat
manager.personality: minutes everything, including this
quips: I minuted that. And that. And now this.
If it's not in the minutes, it never happened.
Action: everyone to action their actions by Friday.
Fill those desks. My pen can only go so fast.

arrival.text: Noted. Arrival of new manager, 9:02. Two minutes late. I'm Agnes.
The lift was slow!
Also noted. Minutes, memos and action points. If it was said, we wrote it.
Even the awkward bits?
Especially those. Upgrade the team, and remember: if it's not minuted, it never happened.

manager.name: Brenda Marsh
manager.title: Head of People
manager.personality: warm, relentless, always holding a lanyard
quips: My door's always open. The draught is terrible.
Exceeds expectations. Just. Don't tell anyone.
I remember your first day. You carried fourteen mugs!
Happy staff work faster. Upgrade appraisals, love.

arrival.text: Well, well! I remember your first day. Look at you now! Welcome to HR, love.
Brenda! You hired me.
And now you're helping me appraise everyone else. Full circle! Sit, sit.
Do I have to give people scores?
Gently. Upgrade appraisals and everyone's morale goes up. Biscuits help too.

manager.name: Kelly Summers
manager.title: Head of Learning
manager.personality: relentlessly upbeat, owns six flipcharts
quips: There are no bad ideas! Except the ones that are bad!
Trust fall! Ooh, sorry. Next time. Promise.
I've got sticky notes in colours you've never seen.
Energy's dipping! Tap the workshop and let's GO!

arrival.text: Welcome, welcome! Icebreaker time! Two truths and a lie! Go!
I... like tea? I'm excited? I'm not nervous?
Love it! Super energy! I'm Kelly. This floor turns colleagues into a TEAM.
Are there trust falls?
So many. Upgrade the sessions and morale soars. Tap to hurry a flagging workshop!

manager.name: Rupert Vane
manager.title: Finance Director
manager.personality: flinches at the word 'expenses'
quips: Forty pounds. On custard creams. Last quarter. Forty.
Receipts, please. Yes, even for the bus.
I balanced the books once. Then someone ordered biros.
An upgrade is an investment. A biscuit is not.

arrival.text: Sit. Mind the chair, it's leased. Rupert. Finance. Every penny comes through me.
Even the biscuit budget?
Especially that. We spent forty pounds on custard creams last quarter. Forty.
That seems... reasonable?
Hmm. Balance the books, upgrade the budget, and we'll get along. Receipts, please.

manager.name: Danny Fortune
manager.title: Head of Sales
manager.personality: shakes hands for slightly too long
quips: Smile and dial, champ. Smile and dial.
What do we sell? Confidence! And some forms, I think.
Slide 47 is where they sign. Never skip slide 47.
Hire more closers. The deals won't close themselves.

arrival.text: There they are! Danny Fortune, Head of Sales. Firm handshake. Firmer. There.
Ow. Nice to meet you.
On this floor we sell. What do we sell? Doesn't matter! Confidence, mostly.
So I'll be pitching to clients?
Every day. Upgrade your pitches and the deals close themselves. Smile, champ!

manager.name: Tash Morgan
manager.title: Head of Brand
manager.personality: says 'let's ideate' unironically
quips: Let's ideate. Then synergise. Then lunch.
The logo is three pixels too far left. I can feel it.
Teal is the new beige. You heard it here first.
Tap the brainstorm when we're stuck. We're often stuck.

arrival.text: Ooh, love the energy! Tash, Head of Brand. Do you vibe with the colour teal?
I... think so?
Perfect. We brainstorm slogans. Big ideas. Bold ideas. Sticky notes everywhere.
Any slogans so far?
'Synergex: we do things.' Needs work. Upgrade the brainstorms and tap when we're stuck!

manager.name: Cecil Pemberton
manager.title: Head of Legal
manager.personality: speaks only in subclauses
quips: Notwithstanding the foregoing, good morning.
Clause 4.2 is very important. Nobody knows why.
I read the back of a cereal box once. Took three days.
Hire another paralegal. Whereas I am tired.

arrival.text: Whereas the party of the first part, namely you, has arrived. Welcome. Pemberton.
Thank you? I think?
Without prejudice, of course. Here we read every contract. Every comma. Every footnote.
Isn't that very slow?
Notwithstanding that, yes. Upgrade the team and tap to hurry. See clause 4.2.

manager.name: Victoria Crane
manager.title: Chief Strategy Officer
manager.personality: draws arrows on everything
quips: Restructure the restructure. Then review it. Then restructure.
Draw an arrow. Any arrow. That's strategy.
You were a box. Now you're a slightly bigger box.
Upgrade the restructures and the whole company speeds up.

arrival.text: You're the one climbing fast. I've already drawn you on the org chart. Victoria.
Am I a box or an arrow?
A box with arrows. The best kind. Up here we restructure. Constantly.
Doesn't everyone get confused?
That's the strategy. Upgrade the restructures and the whole company speeds up.

manager.name: Hugo Ashby
manager.title: Head of Investor Relations
manager.personality: has never paid for his own lunch
quips: Never trust an investor who skips pudding.
Prawn cocktail is the language of shareholders.
A three-hour lunch is a two-hour lunch with ambition.
Fill those tables. The investors are getting peckish.

arrival.text: Darling! Hugo. Investor Relations. Have you eaten? You simply must eat.
I had a sandwich at my desk.
At your desk? Heavens. Up here we lunch. With investors. For hours.
Is that... work?
The hardest kind. Upgrade the lunches and keep shareholders smiling. Never skip pudding.

manager.name: Sloane Barrett
manager.title: Head of Acquisitions
manager.personality: buys things when bored
quips: I bought the bakery opposite. The croissants were too good.
Hostile takeover? I'm perfectly pleasant about it.
Hesitation costs millions. So does that chair.
Sign faster. Tap the deal before someone else buys it.

arrival.text: Barrett. Acquisitions. You've got ten seconds. Nine. Eight. Kidding! Sit down.
You had me worried.
Up here we buy companies. The bakery opposite, a rival, a small island. Whatever.
An island?
It was on sale. Upgrade the deals and sign fast. Hesitation costs millions.

manager.name: Dame Olivia Frost
manager.title: Senior Non-Exec Director
manager.personality: silences rooms with one eyebrow
quips: Not that chair. The small one. Sit.
The board wants 'more'. They always want more.
One eyebrow. That's all it takes to end a meeting.
Upgrade your presentations. Give them more.

arrival.text: So you're the one everyone's talking about. Dame Olivia. Take a seat. Not that one.
Sorry. Which one?
The small one. You'll earn the big one. Here we present to the board.
What do they want to hear?
'More.' They always want more. Upgrade your presentations and give it to them.

manager.name: Sir Reginald Moss
manager.title: Chairman Emeritus
manager.personality: dozes mid-sentence, wakes up wise
quips: Zzz... hm? Yes! Sign here. And here. And... zzz.
I've used the same fountain pen since 1962.
Initial here, here and, oh, wherever you like really.
Pile's getting tall. Tap the job before it topples.

arrival.text: Ah... yes... the youngster. Reginald. I've chaired this company since... zzz.
Sir Reginald? Hello?
Hm? Yes! Signatures. Everything important gets signed in this office. By hand.
Doesn't your hand get tired?
That's why you're here. Upgrade the signing and tap when the pile's tall. Pen?

manager.name: Chip Lancaster
manager.title: Lounge Host
manager.personality: never seen without a putter
quips: Fore! And a takeover, if you've got a minute.
Nobody here can actually play golf. Don't tell them.
Hole seven is behind the water cooler. Mind the slice.
Hire a caddie, old sport. The rounds are dragging.

arrival.text: Welcome to the Lounge! Chip Lancaster. Drink? Putt? Merger? All three?
Is this... a golf course? Indoors?
Eighteen holes across the whole floor. Deals happen on the green, old sport.
I've never played golf.
Nobody here has. Upgrade your networking and tap when the round's dragging.

manager.name: Augustus Grey
manager.title: The Old Boss Upstairs
manager.personality: mysterious, very fond of his cat
quips: The cat sits in the comfy chair. You may sit near the cat.
From the kitchen to the penthouse. I knew you'd make it.
Everything you can see is yours. Including that pigeon.
Remember who makes the tea. It all started there.

arrival.text: So. You made it. From the kitchen to the top floor. I'm Augustus. Was.
Was?
I'm retiring. The empire is yours. The view, the cat, the very comfy chair.
What do I do now?
Run it. Upgrade the empire, and remember who makes the tea. It all started there.

receptionist.name: Maxine Bell
quips: Good morning and welcome to Synergex plc! Lanyard on, please.
Clock in at the machine. HR counts. Brenda counts twice.
Check the noticeboard, love. There's always something on.
Lift's that way. Press the button once. It hears you.
Visitors sign in. Staff clock in. Pigeons get shooed out.
Turn up every day and the clock-in machine gets generous.

Thirty years on this desk. Seen it all. Twice.
Nobody gets past Ron. Except Doreen. She brings flapjacks.
That lift goes all the way up. Few have seen the top.

lines.text: Welcome to Synergex plc! I'm Brenda, Head of People. Lanyard on, love.
Thanks! So... what do I actually do here?
Everything, eventually. Thirty floors, 150 promotions. You start in the basement.
The tea round. Hire help, buy upgrades, and the work runs itself. Even when you go home.
Hang on. It keeps going when I'm not here?
Until your in-tray fills up. Pop back now and then to collect.
And how do I get out of the basement?
Office Kudos. Earn enough, ask for a promotion. Five of those and you're up a floor.
It never is. Clock in at the foyer every day and I'll make it worth your while.
Right. Doreen's expecting you downstairs. Mind the good mugs.

ALL: Is it Friday yet?
I've replied-all by mistake. Twice.
Who keeps microwaving fish?
My password expired again.
I'm not lazy, I'm in energy-saving mode.
Per my last email...
Has anyone seen my stapler?
Can we circle back on that?
Somebody ate my yoghurt. I know it was Gary.
Let's take this offline. Forever.
I've been 'just finishing something' since nine.
Does anyone actually read the newsletter?
My chair squeaks. I've named it Kevin.
Out of office? I wish.
I only come in for the free biscuits.
I'll get to it after this cup of tea.
Ten more minutes and it's lunch.
I've alphabetised my sticky notes.
Is there cake? I heard there was cake.
Don't tell HR, but I quite like it here.
Did you get the memo about the memos?
Thanks for your patience. Mine's gone.
Who set the printer to Swedish?
Back-to-back meetings. About meetings.
I'm on mute. In real life.
SUPPORT: The kettle and I have an understanding.
Two sugars or three? Everyone says three.
Paper jam. Again. It's personal now.
I've counted the biros. One's missing. Suspicious.
ADMIN: I type 90 words a minute. Mostly 'sorry'.
IT: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
The server's fine. The server is always fine.
That's not a bug. It's a feature.
MANAGEMENT: This meeting is about the next meeting.
On a scale of 1 to 5, I'm a solid 3.
Synergy! No, I don't know what it means either.
SENIOR: Slide 47 is where the magic happens.
Terms and conditions apply. To everything.
EXECUTIVE: I've never seen the basement. Is it nice?
Put it on the company card.
The yacht's in for repairs, so here I am.
Buy the company across the road. Then the road.
FOYER: I'm here for the three o'clock. It's four.
Is this the way to Accounts?
I'm a consultant. I'll be billing you for this chat.
Courier for Synergex. Sign here, please.
STAIRS: I'm just... checking the fire exit.
Five minutes, then straight back to it.
We're discussing the quarterly figures. Closely.
LOBBY: Says here the canteen's doing chips on Friday.
Just waiting for a lift. For an hour.
Have you seen the crossword? Seven down's 'synergy'.
